subject: Strategic Acquisition Opportunity – Estonian Consumer Credit Portfolio and Servicing Platform
snippet: Dear, I hope you are well. I am contacting you on behalf of QuickFund regarding a potential strategic acquisition opportunity in the Estonia
body_text:
Dear,

I hope you are well.

I am contacting you on behalf of QuickFund regarding a potential strategic acquisition opportunity in the Estonian consumer credit market. QuickFund is considering a full divestment of its active consumer micro-credit portfolio, together with the proprietary operational infrastructure currently used to originate, monitor, service and collect the portfolio.

This is not a distressed debt sale and not a piecemeal receivables disposal. Our preferred approach is a single transaction covering the full operating package: the receivables portfolio, the customer-facing interface, the internal servicing tools, the repayment tracking system, historical performance data, technical infrastructure, and transition support.

The opportunity may be relevant to a licensed creditor, consumer finance platform, digital lender, credit servicing company, or portfolio purchaser seeking immediate exposure to an existing granular consumer credit portfolio with operational continuity.

Executive summary

QuickFund has built and operated a consumer micro-credit activity in Estonia with a lean internal infrastructure and proprietary servicing technology.

The proposed transaction may include the active consumer credit receivables portfolio, approximately EUR 591,529 of outstanding loan capital, approximately 1,367 borrower relationships, an average exposure of approximately EUR 432.72 per borrower, and an estimated contractual future repayment stream of approximately EUR 667,203 over 24 months.

It may also include the QuickFund customer-facing website and borrower interface, the internal credit servicing and repayment monitoring system, historical repayment and portfolio performance data, operational workflows, collection process documentation, technical infrastructure documentation, and transition support to preserve repayment continuity.

The key value proposition is operational continuity. The buyer would not only acquire a receivables portfolio, but also the system currently used to manage, monitor and collect it.

In practical terms, the platform can be transferred or reconfigured so that existing borrower access remains stable while payment flows, account references, payment provider settings, bank references, webhook endpoints and environment variables are migrated to the acquiring structure, subject to legal, regulatory, payment service provider and data protection requirements.

Strategic rationale

The asset is best understood as a functioning consumer credit servicing platform with an embedded portfolio.

A purely financial buyer may value the portfolio primarily on discounted cash flows. However, a strategic buyer may extract additional value from the existing borrower relationships, customer interface continuity, proprietary internal servicing tools, structured loan and repayment data, reduced integration time, reduced migration friction, immediate repayment monitoring capability, and the potential reuse of the platform for future lending or servicing activity.

Additional value may also come from historical credit performance data and potential integration into an existing consumer finance, debt purchase or credit servicing operation.

This is why we are not positioning the opportunity as a standard distressed receivables sale. We are offering an operating credit asset with its servicing layer.

Portfolio overview

Preliminary internal portfolio data indicates outstanding loan capital of approximately EUR 591,529, with approximately 1,367 borrowers or clients. The average borrower exposure is approximately EUR 432.72.

The indicative average maturity assumption used for modelling is approximately 24 months. Estimated contractual future cash flows over 24 months amount to approximately EUR 667,203, including an estimated future interest component of approximately EUR 75,674.

The portfolio is highly granular. The average borrower exposure is low, reducing single-client concentration risk. This may be attractive for buyers looking for a diversified consumer credit pool rather than a small number of large exposures.

Based on preliminary internal reporting, the year-end identified bad or doubtful amount was approximately EUR 2,425, representing approximately 0.4% of the outstanding loan capital at year-end.

On a full-year basis, internally tracked 2025 bad debt amounted to approximately EUR 25,641, representing approximately 4.3% of year-end outstanding loan capital and approximately 4.9% of average 2025 outstanding capital.

These figures are preliminary and subject to buyer due diligence, loan-level verification and agreed classification methodology.

Financial performance

QuickFund has operated with a lean cost base. The core technology and servicing tools were developed internally by the group, without external software development expenditure.

For financial year 2024, total revenue amounted to EUR 36,630.43. This included EUR 29,629.00 of interest income, EUR 3,521.00 of application fee income, and EUR 3,480.43 of penalty or refund-related income.

Total expenses for 2024 amounted to EUR 7,200.00, resulting in a reported operating profit of EUR 29,430.43 and a reported operating margin of approximately 80.3%.

For financial year 2025, total revenue amounted to EUR 73,184.65. This included EUR 51,725.68 of interest income, EUR 3,521.00 of application fee income, EUR 1,882.97 of penalty or refund-related income, and EUR 16,055.00 of coaching or additional service income.

Total expenses for 2025 amounted to EUR 31,413.68, resulting in a reported operating profit of EUR 41,770.97 and a reported operating margin of approximately 57.1%.

Combined revenue for 2024 and 2025 amounted to EUR 109,815.08. Combined reported operating profit amounted to EUR 71,201.40, with an average reported operating margin of approximately 64.8%.

The historical financials show that the activity has been profitable on an operating basis, while the infrastructure has been built internally and operated with limited external dependency.

Technology and infrastructure

The platform is built around an internally developed operating environment used to manage the credit portfolio and borrower repayment lifecycle. The technical stack can be transferred or documented as part of the transaction.

For the purposes of the initial discussion, the platform should be understood as including a borrower-facing website, a customer interface for repayment visibility, a borrower account area, loan status visibility, a payment and repayment communication layer, and a responsive web interface suitable for consumer use.

On the backend side, the platform includes an internal loan management system, borrower and contract management logic, repayment schedule handling, payment status tracking, portfolio monitoring tools, internal dashboard and reporting logic, borrower-level repayment history, bad debt and late status tracking, and administrative tools for servicing and follow-up.

The database includes borrower-level data structures, loan-level data, repayment schedules, payment history, current balances, contract status, borrower repayment performance, internal status tags, and exportable data for loan tape and due diligence purposes.

The hosting and infrastructure are provided through VM Cloud, the group’s own cloud provider. The infrastructure is controlled internally by the group, with no dependency on a third-party outsourced development agency. The deployment environment is configurable and environment-variable driven, with the capacity to transfer, migrate or document hosting settings depending on the buyer’s preference.

Payments

QuickFund currently uses a combination of payment methods, including Stripe, bank transfers and bank-based repayment flows. The existing infrastructure is designed to track and reconcile payments from several sources.

As part of the transfer, payment routing could be migrated through Stripe configuration transfer or reconfiguration, subject to Stripe approval and compliance checks, as well as through bank account reference updates, beneficiary account changes, repayment instruction updates, payment webhook reconfiguration, internal reconciliation rule updates, borrower communication processes, and transition monitoring to avoid payment disruption.

The technical objective is to make the transfer operationally simple: preserve the customer interface while changing the underlying payment destination and ownership structure in a controlled and compliant manner.

Operational continuity

One of the strongest features of the proposed transaction is continuity.

A buyer may avoid the typical friction of a loan portfolio acquisition where borrowers are suddenly redirected to a new platform, a new interface, a new payment process or a new servicer.

Under the preferred structure, borrowers can continue using the existing customer interface, the website and interface can remain operational, repayment schedules can remain visible, internal tracking can continue, payment references can be migrated, the acquiring entity can gradually take control of servicing, and the seller can provide transition support for a defined period.

This is intended to protect repayment performance and reduce migration risk.

A full transition package could include technical handover, environment documentation, source code or software access depending on the transaction perimeter, database schema and export documentation, deployment procedure, payment flow documentation, Stripe and bank flow transition support, servicing workflow documentation, borrower communication templates, and 30 to 90 days of operational support.

Regulatory and legal positioning

QuickFund currently operates as a credit or micro-credit company engaged in consumer credit origination and servicing. The exact transaction structure can be adapted depending on the buyer’s regulatory status and strategic objective.

One possible structure is a receivables portfolio sale, where the buyer acquires the loan receivables, loan tape, repayment schedules, contract documentation and relevant transferable borrower information.

Another possible structure is a portfolio and platform acquisition, where the buyer acquires the receivables together with the website, customer interface, internal servicing software, technical documentation and transition support.

A third option is a full operating asset transfer, where the buyer acquires the portfolio, servicing platform, software, data structure, operational documentation, brand assets, domain names and transition package.

A corporate transaction may also be discussed if operational continuity, licence treatment, contractual continuity or borrower management is better handled through a share sale or broader corporate acquisition structure.

The exact legal structure would be subject to regulatory, contractual, data protection and tax review. We are prepared to work with the buyer’s legal and compliance teams to identify the most efficient structure.

Data and due diligence materials

Following execution of an NDA, QuickFund can provide a structured due diligence package.

The portfolio data may include a loan-level data tape, borrower-level balances, outstanding capital, accrued or expected interest, repayment schedules, maturity profile, payment history, last payment date, current loan status, borrower segmentation, performing, late and doubtful breakdown, bad debt classification, and cohort-level analysis.

The financial data may include the 2024 P&L summary, the 2025 P&L summary, revenue breakdown, expense breakdown, interest income analysis, application fee income, bad debt data, and bank and payment reconciliation materials where available.

The legal and operational data may include contract templates, borrower communication templates, KYC availability overview, servicing processes, collection workflow, late payment handling, data retention overview, and transfer process considerations.

The technical data may include a platform overview, frontend overview, backend overview, database schema, infrastructure documentation, VM Cloud hosting overview, environment variable structure, payment provider configuration map, Stripe payment flow documentation, bank transfer reconciliation logic, and deployment and migration plan.

Indicative valuation expectation

Given that the opportunity includes both the financial portfolio and the operational servicing infrastructure, QuickFund is not seeking a distressed-debt valuation.

The indicative internal valuation logic is based on outstanding loan capital of approximately EUR 591,529, estimated contractual cash flows over 24 months of approximately EUR 667,203, historical 2024–2025 reported operating profit of approximately EUR 71,201, internally developed servicing technology with no external development cost base, and the inclusion of the existing borrower interface and operational continuity in a full package scenario.

For a portfolio-only transaction, the valuation would be lower and mainly driven by discounted cash-flow analysis, expected losses, servicing costs and buyer target return.

For a full portfolio, platform and operational continuity package, our indicative valuation expectation is in the EUR 650,000 to EUR 700,000 range, depending on the transaction perimeter, level of transition support, treatment of software and IP, data transfer scope, regulatory structure and final due diligence.

For a full operating package including the portfolio, customer-facing interface, internal software, repayment tracking system, technical documentation, data room and transition support, our indicative anchor valuation is approximately EUR 700,000.

This valuation is indicative and subject to due diligence, but it reflects the fact that the buyer is not merely acquiring receivables. The buyer would be acquiring an operating credit servicing environment with an active borrower base and repayment infrastructure already in place.

Why this may be relevant to your organization

We believe this opportunity may be attractive to a buyer that wants to acquire a granular consumer credit portfolio in one transaction, avoid building a servicing platform from scratch, preserve borrower repayment continuity, integrate an existing borrower base, acquire historical repayment data, apply its own funding, collection or credit infrastructure, reduce operational friction compared with a standard portfolio migration, and potentially reuse the technology layer for future credit operations.

For an existing Estonian or Baltic consumer finance operator, the transaction may represent an efficient way to acquire both receivables and operational infrastructure.

Proposed process

We would propose beginning with an introductory discussion to assess strategic fit, followed by execution of an NDA.

After that, QuickFund would provide an initial portfolio summary and technical overview. A management call could then be organized to review the operating model and platform, followed by access to a structured data room.

The buyer would then conduct due diligence and, if interested, submit an indicative non-binding offer. The parties would then discuss the transaction perimeter and legal structure before moving to final due diligence and transaction documentation.

We are seeking a buyer capable of acquiring the full portfolio and operational package in one transaction. We are not looking to sell the portfolio gradually or in small batches.

Please let us know whether this opportunity may be of interest, and who would be the appropriate person within your organization to discuss portfolio acquisitions, consumer credit assets, platform acquisitions or credit servicing opportunities.

Kind regards,

Gaylor Loche
CEO
QuickFund
